newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr rests up for yet another push higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr rests up for yet another push higher.

text.p: Successful defense of key lows last week and Monday's overnight gains leave the dollar in position to move to new highs once again this week, technical analysts said.
Consolidation could continue early this week with a slow grind higher seen distinctly possible, especially against the yen, chartists said.
"Dollar/mark is still congested in a big way," said John Tirone, technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc. "Dollar/yen has been above 120 for six days and a close above 121.45 would be positive."
Dollar/mark seems to have formed a triangle, and possibly even a head-and-shoulders pattern, with a neckline developing near 1.63, chartists noted.

While both formations could point toward an eventual continuation of the move higher, the greenback must first get by stubborn interim resistance at 1.65 marks before it can retest last week's 31-month high at 1.6570, analysts said.

"Dollar/mark had a nice retracement toward 1.6280 and it seems to be on the way up again. But 1.65 was met with strong selling interest," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
Dollar/yen failed to hold 122 on Monday, but could still push past last week's fresh four-year high at 122.80 if support holds at 121.45 and near 121, chartists said.

"I favor a scenario with a dollar move higher above last week's top at 1.2280 yen, which could be broken this week," said Autotte. He cited trendline support at 121 and resistance at 122.30, Friday's high.
Mark/yen has enjoyed a solid bounce from the low 72 area in late January and should make incremental advances as long as it stays above 74, chartists said.
"Mark/yen had a pretty good move last week, breaking above 73.20 and it kept going. The key now is to hold above 74, then start closing above 74.10, 74.20, 74.30," said Tirone.

Despite their relative optimism, chartists said a host of key events and data could keep the dollar in ranges this week. The Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday and Wednesday, UK monetary policy setters meet on Wednesday, U.S. January jobs data debut Friday and G7 leaders meet Saturday in Berlin.
"We could get stuck here. With so many events that people are waiting for, they may not want to take positions right now," Autotte said. (( --Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664 ))
